newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 29.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- The President of the Palestinian Authority, Yasser Arafat, is due in Dublin on Tuesday on the second leg of a tour aimed at winning European support for Palestinians in the Middle East peace talks.
- As tension reportedly increased among loyalist paramilitary prisoners, leaders of the loyalist fringe parties had an emergency meeting with the Northern Secretary, Patrick Mayhew.
- The Irish government may approve proposals to set up a new national food safety agency on Wednesday in an attempt to halt rapidly deteriorating consumer confidence in Ireland's meat industry.
- A significant reduction in state aid would help countries such as Ireland to greatly lower taxes and reduce deficits, Minister for Enterprise and Employment Richard Bruton said.
- An early reduction in interest rates and a less cautious approach to the issue by the Irish Central Bank has been demanded by the Small Firms Association (SFA).
- Authorities in Northern Ireland failed to protect the rights and liberties of people during the summer violence, a new report published by the Committee of Justice (CAJ) claims.
- Irish health authorities went on alert for a new killer strain of the brain sickness CJD on Monday evening following an inquest on its first fatality in Northern Ireland.

- As the various Irish government departments begin to prepare their final budgets for 1997, the Small Firms' Association has issued a sharp criticism of the current administration's lax spending controls and called for significant cuts in public expenditure before the year 2000.
